# Bombadil Property-Based UI Testing — Spike Handoff

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Status:** 🟡 Researched and scoped; prerequisites landed; **nothing Bombadil-specific built yet.**
The demo-seed local-only migration that unblocks it is done and verified. The
remaining work is the dev auto-login and the specification file — see
[Remaining work](#remaining-work).

## The question

Can we run [Bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil) — Antithesis's
property-based testing tool for web UIs — against **only** the local stack, scoped
to a **single page**, with **no receipts reaching Mistral**?

**Answer: yes.** All three constraints are satisfiable. Two of them are not
satisfiable through Bombadil's own configuration, which is the main thing this
document exists to record.

## Use the browser driver, not the terminal one

The spike started from the wrong manual. Bombadil ships two independent drivers:

| Driver      | Docs                                                                   | Drives                      |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| **browser** | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html>  | Anything using the DOM      |
| terminal    | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/terminal/1-introduction.html> | TUIs over stdin/a text grid |

We want **browser**. The terminal manual is a different tool for a different job
and nothing in it transfers.

Useful pages: [specification language](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/3-specification-language.html),
[CLI reference](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/4-reference.html).

## How it works

A loop: extract DOM state → check every property → choose and perform an action →
wait for an event (navigation, DOM mutation, or timeout) → repeat. You supply
properties and action generators as a TypeScript ES module; Bombadil drives the
exploration.

**Four properties come free with no specification at all**: uncaught exceptions,
unhandled promise rejections, error-level console logs, and HTTP 4xx/5xx
responses. Pointing it at a URL with no spec file is a genuinely useful first run.

Specification vocabulary: `extract(state => …)` returns a `Cell<T>` read via
`.current`; formulas are built with `always` / `eventually` / `next` / `now`,
combined with `.and()` / `.or()` / `.implies()` / `.not()`, and time-bounded with
`.within(5, "seconds")`. Action generators are `actions(() => [...])` returning a
weighted tree, with `weighted([[10, a], [1, b]])` to bias exploration. Defaults
live at `@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults`.

Version at time of writing: **v0.6.1**, published 2026-06-18 — comfortably clear of
our `.npmrc` `min-release-age=7`. Exit codes: `0` normal, `1` error, `2` property
violation.

## Three findings that shape the design

### 1. `<ORIGIN>` cannot scope to a single page

The CLI argument is documented as _"Starting URL of the test (also used as a
boundary so that Bombadil doesn't navigate to other websites)"_ — the boundary is
**origin-level**, i.e. `http://localhost:5173`. Passing
`http://localhost:5173/transactions` will **not** stop it wandering into
`/expenses`, `/receipts` or `/profile`.

Single-page confinement therefore has to come from the specification:

- Do **not** `export * from "@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults"` — the defaults
  include general navigation and click-any-semantic-element generators. Re-export
  the default _properties_ only, and hand-write the action generator.
- Add a tripwire property (`always(() => location.pathname === "/transactions")`)
  so an escape is a loud violation rather than silent scope creep.

### 2. There is no network interception, blocking, or mocking

Nothing in the CLI or the specification language stubs outbound requests. Keeping
receipts away from Mistral is an application-level concern, and fortunately a
narrow one: the browser's **only** Mistral touchpoint is
`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` → `POST /api/ocr/extract`. A page that
never uploads a receipt never reaches it.

Belt and braces: run the dev server with **no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`**. It is a dynamic
import (see the comment in `playwright.config.ts`), so the endpoint fails at
request time rather than build time — which turns the free "no 5xx responses"
property into a tripwire. If Bombadil ever finds a path to OCR, we get a
violation instead of a silent API bill.

### 3. There is no authentication support

No `--storage-state`, no cookie flag, no login helper. `--header` injects HTTP
headers only, which is useless here: `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` uses plain
`createClient` with `persistSession: true`, so the session lives in
**localStorage**.

Two ways out, and we chose the second:

- **`bombadil browser test-external --remote-debugger http://localhost:9222`** —
  launch your own Chromium, log in by hand, attach Bombadil to the live tab.
  Rejected: it depends on `--create-target=false` attaching to the _existing_
  authenticated tab, which the docs do not confirm, and it needs manual
  choreography before every run.
- **A dev-only auto-login** ✅ — establish a real Supabase session at boot. Auth
  stays fully intact, plain `bombadil browser test` works, and the run is
  reproducible from one command.

Note this deliberately means Bombadil never explores the logged-out state or the
login page. Acceptable given the single-page scope; revisit if the scope widens.

## Why not a true auth bypass

Considered and rejected. Every protected page independently calls
`supabase.auth.getSession()`, and all reads are RLS-gated on `family_members`.
Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.

## Target page: `/transactions`

`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.

Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
disagree.

**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
less state worth exploring.

**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs.

## Prerequisites — done

Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:

- Demo family torn down in production; verified by direct SQL (demo users, demo
  family, and orphan sweeps across every family/user-scoped table plus
  `storage.objects` — all zero).
- `readConfig()` hard-fails on any non-loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, before the
  service-role client is built.
- Demo password is now the checked-in constant `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
  `scripts/demo/common.ts` (`DemoFamily-2026!local`), verified to authenticate
  against the local stack.
- Script names simplified — `npm run dev` and `npm run seed:demo` are the local
  ones; production is the explicit `npm run dev:remote`.
- `npm run check` now type-checks `scripts/` and `e2e/`, which it never did before.

See [Demo data seed](../demo-seed.md) and [Local development](../local-dev.md).

## Remaining work

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + hook in `src/routes/+layout.svelte:28`.**
   Must complete _before_ `authChecked = true`, or the layout briefly treats the
   user as logged out and the run starts with a redirect flap.

   Gate on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops plain
   `npm run dev`… — which is now local, but `dev:remote` is still DEV — from firing
   demo credentials at production.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`. Reset-to-known-state matters
   more here than in normal dev: `--reproduce` only replays faithfully from an
   identical starting state, and the docs are explicit that reproductions fail when
   "application state has changed".

3. **The specification** — `bombadil/transactions.ts`. Default properties only (no
   `export *`), a hand-written action generator confined to the page's own
   controls, the pathname tripwire, and the filter/sort properties above.

4. **Decide where it runs.** Local-only for now. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs.

## Suggested first run

Deliberately with **no specification file** — just to confirm the binary installs
and the free properties report before investing in a spec:

```bash
npm run db:up
npm run seed:demo
npm run dev                    # localhost:5173, no MISTRAL_API_KEY
npx bombadil browser test --time-limit 2m --output-path bombadil-out \
  http://localhost:5173/login
npx bombadil browser inspect bombadil-out   # timeline UI, violation markers
```

Then repeat against `/transactions` once auto-login lands, adding the spec file as
the final argument.

## Ruled out — do not redo

- **The terminal driver.** Wrong tool; it drives TUIs.
- **Scoping to one page via `<ORIGIN>`.** Origin-level only; must be done in the spec.
- **Network mocking to block Mistral.** Bombadil has no such feature.
- **`--header` for authentication.** The session is in localStorage, not a header.
- **A true auth/RLS bypass.** Yields an empty shell and a test-only code path.
- **`test-external` + remote debugger.** Viable fallback, but unverified and manual;
  superseded by auto-login.
- **Re-logging-in on `SIGNED_OUT`.** Masks real session-loss bugs.

## Open questions

- Does `--create-target=false` attach to an existing authenticated tab? Unresolved —
  only matters if we fall back to `test-external`.
- No documented `--seed` flag for the browser driver, despite the terminal driver
  having one. Reproduction is via `--reproduce <TRACE>` instead. Worth re-checking
  on a later release.
- Auth support was a known gap as of v0.3.2 and is still undocumented at v0.6.1.
  If upstream adds it, the auto-login may become unnecessary.

</context>

## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## Core Behavior

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- seo-optimizer: Optimize content for search engines with keyword analysis, readability scoring, meta descriptions, and competitor comparison. Use this when users want to improve SEO, optimize blog posts, or analyze content for search performance.
- systems-thinking: Analyze problems using a Systems Thinking approach. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Guides conversation through questions and observations rather than prescriptive solutions.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Bombadil Property-Based UI Testing — Spike Handoff

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Status:** 🟡 Researched and scoped; prerequisites landed; **nothing Bombadil-specific built yet.**
The demo-seed local-only migration that unblocks it is done and verified. The
remaining work is the dev auto-login and the specification file — see
[Remaining work](#remaining-work).

## The question

Can we run [Bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil) — Antithesis's
property-based testing tool for web UIs — against **only** the local stack, scoped
to a **single page**, with **no receipts reaching Mistral**?

**Answer: yes.** All three constraints are satisfiable. Two of them are not
satisfiable through Bombadil's own configuration, which is the main thing this
document exists to record.

## Use the browser driver, not the terminal one

The spike started from the wrong manual. Bombadil ships two independent drivers:

| Driver      | Docs                                                                   | Drives                      |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| **browser** | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html>  | Anything using the DOM      |
| terminal    | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/terminal/1-introduction.html> | TUIs over stdin/a text grid |

We want **browser**. The terminal manual is a different tool for a different job
and nothing in it transfers.

Useful pages: [specification language](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/3-specification-language.html),
[CLI reference](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/4-reference.html).

## How it works

A loop: extract DOM state → check every property → choose and perform an action →
wait for an event (navigation, DOM mutation, or timeout) → repeat. You supply
properties and action generators as a TypeScript ES module; Bombadil drives the
exploration.

**Four properties come free with no specification at all**: uncaught exceptions,
unhandled promise rejections, error-level console logs, and HTTP 4xx/5xx
responses. Pointing it at a URL with no spec file is a genuinely useful first run.

Specification vocabulary: `extract(state => …)` returns a `Cell<T>` read via
`.current`; formulas are built with `always` / `eventually` / `next` / `now`,
combined with `.and()` / `.or()` / `.implies()` / `.not()`, and time-bounded with
`.within(5, "seconds")`. Action generators are `actions(() => [...])` returning a
weighted tree, with `weighted([[10, a], [1, b]])` to bias exploration. Defaults
live at `@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults`.

Version at time of writing: **v0.6.1**, published 2026-06-18 — comfortably clear of
our `.npmrc` `min-release-age=7`. Exit codes: `0` normal, `1` error, `2` property
violation.

## Three findings that shape the design

### 1. `<ORIGIN>` cannot scope to a single page

The CLI argument is documented as _"Starting URL of the test (also used as a
boundary so that Bombadil doesn't navigate to other websites)"_ — the boundary is
**origin-level**, i.e. `http://localhost:5173`. Passing
`http://localhost:5173/transactions` will **not** stop it wandering into
`/expenses`, `/receipts` or `/profile`.

Single-page confinement therefore has to come from the specification:

- Do **not** `export * from "@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults"` — the defaults
  include general navigation and click-any-semantic-element generators. Re-export
  the default _properties_ only, and hand-write the action generator.
- Add a tripwire property (`always(() => location.pathname === "/transactions")`)
  so an escape is a loud violation rather than silent scope creep.

### 2. There is no network interception, blocking, or mocking

Nothing in the CLI or the specification language stubs outbound requests. Keeping
receipts away from Mistral is an application-level concern, and fortunately a
narrow one: the browser's **only** Mistral touchpoint is
`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` → `POST /api/ocr/extract`. A page that
never uploads a receipt never reaches it.

Belt and braces: run the dev server with **no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`**. It is a dynamic
import (see the comment in `playwright.config.ts`), so the endpoint fails at
request time rather than build time — which turns the free "no 5xx responses"
property into a tripwire. If Bombadil ever finds a path to OCR, we get a
violation instead of a silent API bill.

### 3. There is no authentication support

No `--storage-state`, no cookie flag, no login helper. `--header` injects HTTP
headers only, which is useless here: `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` uses plain
`createClient` with `persistSession: true`, so the session lives in
**localStorage**.

Two ways out, and we chose the second:

- **`bombadil browser test-external --remote-debugger http://localhost:9222`** —
  launch your own Chromium, log in by hand, attach Bombadil to the live tab.
  Rejected: it depends on `--create-target=false` attaching to the _existing_
  authenticated tab, which the docs do not confirm, and it needs manual
  choreography before every run.
- **A dev-only auto-login** ✅ — establish a real Supabase session at boot. Auth
  stays fully intact, plain `bombadil browser test` works, and the run is
  reproducible from one command.

Note this deliberately means Bombadil never explores the logged-out state or the
login page. Acceptable given the single-page scope; revisit if the scope widens.

## Why not a true auth bypass

Considered and rejected. Every protected page independently calls
`supabase.auth.getSession()`, and all reads are RLS-gated on `family_members`.
Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.

## Target page: `/transactions`

`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.

Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
disagree.

**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
less state worth exploring.

**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs.

## Prerequisites — done

Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:

- Demo family torn down in production; verified by direct SQL (demo users, demo
  family, and orphan sweeps across every family/user-scoped table plus
  `storage.objects` — all zero).
- `readConfig()` hard-fails on any non-loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, before the
  service-role client is built.
- Demo password is now the checked-in constant `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
  `scripts/demo/common.ts` (`DemoFamily-2026!local`), verified to authenticate
  against the local stack.
- Script names simplified — `npm run dev` and `npm run seed:demo` are the local
  ones; production is the explicit `npm run dev:remote`.
- `npm run check` now type-checks `scripts/` and `e2e/`, which it never did before.

See [Demo data seed](../demo-seed.md) and [Local development](../local-dev.md).

## Remaining work

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + hook in `src/routes/+layout.svelte:28`.**
   Must complete _before_ `authChecked = true`, or the layout briefly treats the
   user as logged out and the run starts with a redirect flap.

   Gate on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops plain
   `npm run dev`… — which is now local, but `dev:remote` is still DEV — from firing
   demo credentials at production.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`. Reset-to-known-state matters
   more here than in normal dev: `--reproduce` only replays faithfully from an
   identical starting state, and the docs are explicit that reproductions fail when
   "application state has changed".

3. **The specification** — `bombadil/transactions.ts`. Default properties only (no
   `export *`), a hand-written action generator confined to the page's own
   controls, the pathname tripwire, and the filter/sort properties above.

4. **Decide where it runs.** Local-only for now. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs.

## Suggested first run

Deliberately with **no specification file** — just to confirm the binary installs
and the free properties report before investing in a spec:

```bash
npm run db:up
npm run seed:demo
npm run dev                    # localhost:5173, no MISTRAL_API_KEY
npx bombadil browser test --time-limit 2m --output-path bombadil-out \
  http://localhost:5173/login
npx bombadil browser inspect bombadil-out   # timeline UI, violation markers
```

Then repeat against `/transactions` once auto-login lands, adding the spec file as
the final argument.

## Ruled out — do not redo

- **The terminal driver.** Wrong tool; it drives TUIs.
- **Scoping to one page via `<ORIGIN>`.** Origin-level only; must be done in the spec.
- **Network mocking to block Mistral.** Bombadil has no such feature.
- **`--header` for authentication.** The session is in localStorage, not a header.
- **A true auth/RLS bypass.** Yields an empty shell and a test-only code path.
- **`test-external` + remote debugger.** Viable fallback, but unverified and manual;
  superseded by auto-login.
- **Re-logging-in on `SIGNED_OUT`.** Masks real session-loss bugs.

## Open questions

- Does `--create-target=false` attach to an existing authenticated tab? Unresolved —
  only matters if we fall back to `test-external`.
- No documented `--seed` flag for the browser driver, despite the terminal driver
  having one. Reproduction is via `--reproduce <TRACE>` instead. Worth re-checking
  on a later release.
- Auth support was a known gap as of v0.3.2 and is still undocumented at v0.6.1.
  If upstream adds it, the auto-login may become unnecessary.

3	A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
4	development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.
5

7	
8	1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
9	   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
10	   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.
11	
12	   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
13	   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
14	   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
15	   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
16	   itself.
17	
18	2. `npm install`
19	
20	## Daily use
21	
22	```bash
23	npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
24	npm run dev          # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
25	```
26	
27	| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
28	| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
29	| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
30	| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
31	| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
32	| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
33	| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
34	| `npm run dev:remote`       | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
35	| `npm run seed:demo`        | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
36	| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |
37	
38	`dev` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
39	key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
40	every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
41	1Password. Only `npm run dev:remote` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.
42	
43	**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
44	swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
45	reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
46	
47	Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
48	That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
49	OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.
50	
51	Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.
52	
53	## Getting data to look at
54	
55	```bash
56	npm run seed:demo
57	```
58	
59	Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
60	Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
61	to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
62	
63	A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo`.
64	
65	## The schema baseline
66	
67	`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.
68	
69	The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
70	were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
71	died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
72	`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
73	`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
74	cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.
75	
76	The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
77	storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
78	`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
79	that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.
80	
81	Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
82	baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
83	`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
84	date.
85	
86	From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
87	verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.
88	
89	## Testing
90	
91	- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
92	- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
93	  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
94	- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
95	  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
96	  baseline these could never run at all.
97	
98	## What still is not local
99	
100	- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
101	  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
102	  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
103	- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
104	  your machine.
105	
106	## Troubleshooting
107	
108	- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
109	  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
110	- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
111	  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
112	  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
113	- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
114	  take seconds.

# Local development

A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.

## One-time setup

1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.

   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
   itself.

2. `npm install`

## Daily use

```bash
npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
npm run dev          # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
```

| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
| `npm run dev:remote`       | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
| `npm run seed:demo`        | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |

`dev` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
1Password. Only `npm run dev:remote` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.

**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo`.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

# Bombadil Getting Started Steps

## Installation

For npm projects, install as a dev dependency:
```bash
npm install --save-dev @antithesishq/bombadil
```

Add to `package.json`:
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "bombadil browser test --time-limit=1m https://your-app.example.com"
  }
}
```

## First Run Command

After installation, execute a test against a sample site:
```bash
bombadil browser test https://en.wikipedia.org --output-path my-test
```

Then inspect results:
```bash
bombadil browser inspect my-test
```

## First Specification File

**Note:** The provided documentation does not include a complete example specification file with its exports in the "Getting started" section. The page references the "[Specification language](3-specification-language.html#specification-language)" section for examples, but those details are not included in the excerpt provided. To view actual specification code examples with exports, you would need to consult section 3 of the manual directly.

1	/**
2	 * Bombadil specification for the Transactions page (#{#bmb1a}).
3	 *
4	 * Run with `npm run bombadil` (see docs/plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
5	 * Requires the local stack seeded and `npm run dev` running — the dev-only
6	 * auto-login in `src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` supplies the session, because
7	 * Bombadil has no authentication support of its own.
8	 *
9	 * ## Why this file is hand-written rather than `export *`-ing the defaults
10	 *
11	 * `<ORIGIN>` is an *origin* boundary, not a page boundary: passing
12	 * `http://localhost:5173/transactions` does nothing to stop Bombadil wandering
13	 * into `/expenses` or `/profile`. Single-page confinement has to come from the
14	 * specification, so we re-export the default *properties* only and enumerate
15	 * every action target ourselves. `pageIsAlwaysTransactions` below is the
16	 * tripwire that turns an escape into a loud violation instead of silent scope
17	 * creep.
18	 *
19	 * ## What is deliberately NOT clickable, and why
20	 *
21	 * - **The whole `<header>`.** It holds Logout. One click and the rest of the run
22	 *   explores `/login`. Every target is found under `<main>`.
23	 * - **The import card.** Its file input opens a native OS file chooser, which
24	 *   nothing in the page can dismiss — the run would simply hang.
25	 * - **Row `Delete` and `Delete Selected`.** Two reasons. They call `confirm()`,
26	 *   a modal browser dialog outside the DOM that the action vocabulary cannot
27	 *   answer; and they destroy the seeded rows the run needs, which also breaks
28	 *   `--reproduce` (it replays faithfully only from an identical start state).
29	 * - **`Back` / `Forward` / `Reload`.** All three leave or reset the page under
30	 *   test for no exploratory gain.
31	 * - **`Tab`.** Focus traversal walks straight out of `<main>` and into the
32	 *   header's Logout button, where a subsequent `Enter` ends the run.
33	 *
34	 * Receipt OCR is unreachable from here — the page never uploads a receipt, and
35	 * the only browser-side Mistral touchpoint is `ReceiptService`'s
36	 * `POST /api/ocr/extract`. Belt and braces, `npm run dev` sets no
37	 * `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so the endpoint 500s if it is ever reached and the free
38	 * `noHttpErrorCodes` property fires.
39	 *
40	 * ## A note on cost
41	 *
42	 * Extractors run on **every** state, and this page renders ~100 rows. Anything
43	 * that measures geometry (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getComputedStyle`) forces
44	 * layout, so doing it per candidate element is the difference between a usable
45	 * run and one that crawls. Hence the single `pageTargets` extractor: one DOM
46	 * pass produces every action target, rows off-screen are rejected before their
47	 * cells are ever measured, and the property extractors below touch no geometry
48	 * at all.
49	 */
50	import { always, from, not } from '@antithesishq/bombadil';
51	import { actions, extract, weighted } from '@antithesishq/bombadil/browser';
52	import type { Action, State } from '@antithesishq/bombadil/browser';
53	
54	/** The four free properties: no uncaught exceptions, rejections, console errors or 4xx/5xx. */
55	export {
56		noConsoleErrors,
57		noHttpErrorCodes,
58		noUncaughtExceptions,
59		noUnhandledPromiseRejections
60	} from '@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults';
61	
62	const PAGE_PATH = '/transactions';
63	
64	const ROW_SELECTOR = 'tbody tr[role="button"]';
65	const CALENDAR = '[role="dialog"][aria-label="Calendar"]';
66	
67	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68	// DOM helpers
69	//
70	// Extractors may only return JSON, so nothing here hands back an Element — the
71	// element hunting happens inside the extractor and only names, labels and
72	// coordinates come out.
73	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	
75	type Point = { x: number; y: number };
76	/** A thing worth clicking: a label for the trace plus where to click it. */
77	type Target = { name: string; content: string; point: Point };
78	
79	function textOf(element: Element): string {
80		return (element.textContent ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
81	}
82	
83	function queryAll(root: Element, selector: string): Element[] {
84		return Array.from(root.querySelectorAll(selector));
85	}
86	
87	/** Buttons whose visible label starts with `prefix` — for controls with no id or aria-label. */
88	function buttonsLabelled(root: Element, prefix: string): Element[] {
89		return queryAll(root, 'button').filter((button) => textOf(button).startsWith(prefix));
90	}
91	
92	/** The page body. Every target is found under it, so the header is unreachable. */
93	function main(state: State): Element | null {
94		return state.document.querySelector('main');
95	}
96	
97	/**
98	 * The Edit Transaction dialog's panel, when it is open. Found by its heading
99	 * rather than its utility classes, which are Tailwind noise and change freely.
100	 */
101	function editDialog(root: Element): Element | null {
102		for (const heading of root.querySelectorAll('h3')) {
103			if (textOf(heading) === 'Edit Transaction') return heading.parentElement;
104		}
105		return null;
106	}
107	
108	/**
109	 * Where to click `element`, or null if clicking it would be meaningless:
110	 * disabled, zero-sized, or scrolled out of the viewport. Bombadil dispatches at
111	 * a coordinate, so an off-screen target would land on whatever is there instead.
112	 */
113	function clickPoint(state: State, element: Element): Point | null {
114		if ('disabled' in element && element.disabled === true) return null;
115	
116		const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
117		if (rect.width <= 0 || rect.height <= 0) return null;
118	
119		const point = { x: rect.left + rect.width / 2, y: rect.top + rect.height / 2 };
120		const onScreen =
121			point.x >= 0 &&
122			point.y >= 0 &&
123			point.x < state.window.innerWidth &&
124			point.y < state.window.innerHeight;
125	
126		return onScreen ? point : null;
127	}
128	
129	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	// Action targets — one DOM pass, grouped by control
131	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
132	
133	const GROUPS = [
134		'filter-input',
135		'filter-cardtype',
136		'filter-button',
137		'show-excluded',
138		'datepicker',
139		'calendar',
140		'select',
141		'clear-selection',
142		'sort',
143		'row',
144		'exclude',
145		'dismiss',
146		'dialog-field',
147		'dialog-button',
148		'dialog-calendar'
149	] as const;
150	
151	type Group = (typeof GROUPS)[number];
152	type Targets = Record<string, Target[]>;
153	
154	/**
155	 * Every clickable target on the page, keyed by control group.
156	 *
157	 * The dialog is a modal overlay, so the two worlds are mutually exclusive:
158	 * while it is open only `dialog-*` groups are populated, otherwise only the
159	 * page groups are. Without that split most generated clicks would land on the
160	 * backdrop while the dialog was up.
161	 */
162	const pageTargets = extract((state): Targets => {
163		const found: Targets = {};
164		for (const group of GROUPS) found[group] = [];
165	
166		const body = main(state);
167		if (!body) return found;
168	
169		const collect = (group: Group, elements: Iterable<Element>) => {
170			const list = found[group];
171			for (const element of elements) {
172				const point = clickPoint(state, element);
173				if (point) list.push({ name: `${group}[${list.length}]`, content: textOf(element), point });
174			}
175		};
176	
177		const dialog = editDialog(body);
178		if (dialog) {
179			collect(
180				'dialog-field',
181				queryAll(dialog, 'input, select, button[aria-label="Open date picker"]')
182			);
183			collect('dialog-button', [
184				...buttonsLabelled(dialog, 'Cancel'),
185				...buttonsLabelled(dialog, 'Save')
186			]);
187			collect(
188				'dialog-calendar',
189				queryAll(dialog, `${CALENDAR} [role="gridcell"]:not([aria-disabled="true"])`)
190			);
191			return found;
192		}
193	
194		collect(
195			'filter-input',
196			queryAll(body, '#tx-filter-vendor, #tx-filter-amount-min, #tx-filter-amount-max')
197		);
198

# Demo Data Seed

A re-runnable script that populates a self-contained **"Sample Family (DEMO)"**
in the **local** Supabase stack, so the running app can be logged into for
documentation screenshots/videos and manual exploratory testing.

> **Local only.** The demo family was also seeded into the remote project until
> 2026-07-26, when it was torn down there and the remote scripts were removed.
> `readConfig()` now refuses any non-loopback target.

It is deliberately **image-free**: every seeded receipt has
`receipt_image_path = null`, so receipts render in their placeholder state
("No image" / "(manual)"). See the note on that below.

> **Reuse:** the seed is written so a future automated test harness can reuse
> the same fixtures. That harness is **not** built yet — this is a dev utility
> today.

## Logins

| Role   | Email                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Owner  | `sample.parent@example.com`  |
| Member | `sample.partner@example.com` |

Both share one family and one **fixed password**, `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
`scripts/demo/common.ts`, also printed at the end of each seed run.
`@example.com` is an IANA-reserved documentation domain — it accepts no mail and
can't collide with real accounts.

The password used to be randomly generated per run. It is a checked-in constant
now so local tooling can log in unattended, which is only safe because the demo
account cannot exist anywhere but a loopback stack — see the guard below.

## Commands

```bash
npm run seed:demo            # auto-clean any prior demo data, then rebuild
npm run seed:demo:teardown   # delete the demo users + demo family
```

Both wrap `local:env`, which injects Supabase's fixed local defaults, so neither
needs 1Password. They need:

- `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the target stack (echoed on start).
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — full-access key; required to create the auth
  users (Admin API) and to insert RLS-protected rows. The scripts hard-fail with
  a clear message if either is missing.

## The local-only guard

`readConfig()` rejects any `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` whose hostname is not loopback,
before the service-role client is built. That is what makes a checked-in
password acceptable: seeding a remote project would plant a known credential in
it, so "don't do that" is enforced rather than agreed. Relaxing the guard means
reinstating a generated password.

A full local wipe is `npm run db:reset` — `seed:demo:teardown` exists for
removing just the demo family while leaving the rest of your local data intact.

`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).

**Teardown order matters:** `teardownDemo()` must delete the **auth users before
the family**. `receipts.family_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and receipts only
cascade via `receipts.user_id` — so deleting the family first leaves the demo
receipts alive with a nulled `family_id`, invisible to the name-scoped cleanup
and un-removable by a re-run.

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.
- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

## The no-image consequence

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

## Files

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).

33:## Engineering
34-
35-### In progress
36-
37-- **🟡 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike).** Researched and scoped 2026-07-26; prerequisites landed, nothing Bombadil-specific built. Feasible against the local stack with all three constraints met (local-only, single page, no Mistral), but two of them can't be met through Bombadil's own config: `<ORIGIN>` bounds navigation at the **origin**, not the path, so single-page scoping has to be done in the spec; and there is **no network mocking**, so Mistral is avoided by page choice plus running with no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. Auth is undocumented at v0.6.1 and the session lives in localStorage, so the plan is a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login rather than `test-external`. Target page `/transactions`. Remaining: `src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + layout hook, `db:fresh`, and the specification file. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
38-
39-### Security
40-
41-- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
42-- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
43-- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.
44-
45-### Dependencies
46-
47-- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
48-- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
49-
50-### Correctness / infrastructure
51-
52-- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.** The [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md) got `npm run check` to 0 errors / 0 warnings (down from 118), but its second goal — making the type check a _required CI gate so it can't silently regress_ — is unmet: the repo has **no CI at all** (`.github/workflows/` does not exist). Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. Stand up a workflow (GitHub Actions is the natural fit) running at least `npm run check` on every PR and blocking merge on failure; fold in `npm run lint` and `npm test` while there. CI installs must use `npm ci` (honours the lockfile; `min-release-age` gates resolution, not `ci`). This is the last open deliverable of that PRD.
53-- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
54-- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
55-- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
56-- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
57-- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
58-- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

63-follow-ups **RV-01→11**) has landed — see [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md)

47-- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
48-- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
49-
50-### Correctness / infrastructure
51-
52-- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.** The [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md) got `npm run check` to 0 errors / 0 warnings (down from 118), but its second goal — making the type check a _required CI gate so it can't silently regress_ — is unmet: the repo has **no CI at all** (`.github/workflows/` does not exist). Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. Stand up a workflow (GitHub Actions is the natural fit) running at least `npm run check` on every PR and blocking merge on failure; fold in `npm run lint` and `npm test` while there. CI installs must use `npm ci` (honours the lockfile; `min-release-age` gates resolution, not `ci`). This is the last open deliverable of that PRD.
53-- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
54-- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
55-- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
56-- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
57-- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
58-- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.
59-

content.text: While that runs, updating the docs. First the backlog — the audit surfaced new vulnerabilities:

content.content:
30	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
31	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).
32	
33	## Engineering
34	
35	### In progress
36	
37	- **🟡 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike).** Researched and scoped 2026-07-26; prerequisites landed, nothing Bombadil-specific built. Feasible against the local stack with all three constraints met (local-only, single page, no Mistral), but two of them can't be met through Bombadil's own config: `<ORIGIN>` bounds navigation at the **origin**, not the path, so single-page scoping has to be done in the spec; and there is **no network mocking**, so Mistral is avoided by page choice plus running with no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. Auth is undocumented at v0.6.1 and the session lives in localStorage, so the plan is a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login rather than `test-external`. Target page `/transactions`. Remaining: `src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + layout hook, `db:fresh`, and the specification file. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
38	
39	### Security
40	
41	- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
42	- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way.
