- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

### In progress

- **🟡 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike).** Researched and scoped 2026-07-26; prerequisites landed, nothing Bombadil-specific built. Feasible against the local stack with all three constraints met (local-only, single page, no Mistral), but two of them can't be met through Bombadil's own config: `<ORIGIN>` bounds navigation at the **origin**, not the path, so single-page scoping has to be done in the spec; and there is **no network mocking**, so Mistral is avoided by page choice plus running with no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. Auth is undocumented at v0.6.1 and the session lives in localStorage, so the plan is a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login rather than `test-external`. Target page `/transactions`. Remaining: `src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + layout hook, `db:fresh`, and the specification file. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

### Dependencies

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

# Demo Data Seed

A re-runnable script that populates a self-contained **"Sample Family (DEMO)"**
in the **local** Supabase stack, so the running app can be logged into for
documentation screenshots/videos and manual exploratory testing.

> **Local only.** The demo family was also seeded into the remote project until
> 2026-07-26, when it was torn down there and the remote scripts were removed.
> `readConfig()` now refuses any non-loopback target.

It is deliberately **image-free**: every seeded receipt has
`receipt_image_path = null`, so receipts render in their placeholder state
("No image" / "(manual)"). See the note on that below.

> **Reuse:** the seed is written so a future automated test harness can reuse
> the same fixtures. That harness is **not** built yet — this is a dev utility
> today.

## Logins

| Role   | Email                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Owner  | `sample.parent@example.com`  |
| Member | `sample.partner@example.com` |

Both share one family and one **fixed password**, `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
`scripts/demo/common.ts`, also printed at the end of each seed run.
`@example.com` is an IANA-reserved documentation domain — it accepts no mail and
can't collide with real accounts.

The password used to be randomly generated per run. It is a checked-in constant
now so local tooling can log in unattended, which is only safe because the demo
account cannot exist anywhere but a loopback stack — see the guard below.

## Commands

```bash
npm run seed:demo            # auto-clean any prior demo data, then rebuild
npm run seed:demo:teardown   # delete the demo users + demo family
```

Both wrap `local:env`, which injects Supabase's fixed local defaults, so neither
needs 1Password. They need:

- `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the target stack (echoed on start).
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — full-access key; required to create the auth
  users (Admin API) and to insert RLS-protected rows. The scripts hard-fail with
  a clear message if either is missing.

## The local-only guard

`readConfig()` rejects any `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` whose hostname is not loopback,
before the service-role client is built. That is what makes a checked-in
password acceptable: seeding a remote project would plant a known credential in
it, so "don't do that" is enforced rather than agreed. Relaxing the guard means
reinstating a generated password.

A full local wipe is `npm run db:reset` — `seed:demo:teardown` exists for
removing just the demo family while leaving the rest of your local data intact.

`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).

**Teardown order matters:** `teardownDemo()` must delete the **auth users before
the family**. `receipts.family_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and receipts only
cascade via `receipts.user_id` — so deleting the family first leaves the demo
receipts alive with a nulled `family_id`, invisible to the name-scoped cleanup
and un-removable by a re-run.

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.
- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

## The no-image consequence

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

## Files

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).

and un-removable by a re-run.

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.

  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

# Local development

A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.

## One-time setup

1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.

   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
   itself.

2. `npm install`

## Daily use

```bash
npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
npm run dev          # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
```

| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
| `npm run dev:remote`       | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
| `npm run seed:demo`        | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |

`dev` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
1Password. Only `npm run dev:remote` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.

**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo`.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

sessions.

**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:fresh`.

**You will already be logged in.** In dev, against a loopback stack, the app signs itself in as the
demo owner at boot (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`) — it exists so Bombadil, which cannot authenticate
itself, gets a real session. Two gates, for two reasons: `import.meta.env.DEV` is what keeps the
password out of the production bundle (verified — it is dead-code-eliminated), and the loopback
check is what stops `dev:remote`, which is also DEV, from firing demo credentials at production. To
see the logged-out screens, go to `/login` directly; the auto-login skips the auth routes, so a
manual logout sticks.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

1	# Local development
2	
3	A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
4	development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.
5	
6	## One-time setup
7	
8	1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
9	   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
10	   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.
11	
12	   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
13	   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
14	   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
15	   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
16	   itself.
17	
18	2. `npm install`
19	
20	## Daily use
21	
22	```bash
23	npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
24	npm run dev          # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
25	```
26	
27	| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
28	| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
29	| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
30	| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
31	| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
32	| `npm run db:fresh`         | `db:reset` then `seed:demo` — back to a known state in one command   |
33	| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
34	| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
35	| `npm run dev:remote`       | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
36	| `npm run seed:demo`        | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
37	| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |
38	| `npm run bombadil`         | Property-based UI exploration of `/transactions` (see below)         |
39	
40	`dev` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
41	key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
42	every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
43	1Password. Only `npm run dev:remote` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.
44	
45	**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
46	swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
47	reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
48	
49	Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
50	That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
51	OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.
52	
53	Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.
54	
55	## Getting data to look at
56	
57	```bash
58	npm run seed:demo
59	```
60	
61	Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
62	Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
63	to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
64	
65	A clean slate is `npm run db:fresh`.
66	
67	**You will already be logged in.** In dev, against a loopback stack, the app signs itself in as the
68	demo owner at boot (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`) — it exists so Bombadil, which cannot authenticate
69	itself, gets a real session. Two gates, for two reasons: `import.meta.env.DEV` is what keeps the
70	password out of the production bundle (verified — it is dead-code-eliminated), and the loopback
71	check is what stops `dev:remote`, which is also DEV, from firing demo credentials at production. To
72	see the logged-out screens, go to `/login` directly; the auto-login skips the auth routes, so a
73	manual logout sticks.
74	
75	## The schema baseline
76	
77	`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.
78	
79	The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
80	were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
81	died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
82	`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
83	`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
84	cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.
85	
86	The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
87	storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
88	`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
89	that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.
90	
91	Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
92	baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
93	`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
94	date.
95	
96	From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
97	verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.
98	
99	## Testing
100	
101	- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
102	- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
103	  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
104	- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
105	  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
106	  baseline these could never run at all.
107	
108	## Property-based UI exploration (Bombadil)
109	
110	```bash
111	npm run db:fresh     # known starting state — --reproduce depends on it
112	npm run dev          # in another terminal
113	npm run bombadil     # explore /transactions; exit 2 means a property was violated
114	npm run bombadil:inspect
115	```
116	
117	Antithesis's [Bombadil](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html) drives
118	the page at random and checks the properties in `bombadil/transactions.ts` after every action. That
119	file is the interesting part — read its header before changing it, because most of what is _not_ in
120	it (the header, the file input, every `<select>`, the Delete buttons) is excluded for a reason that
121	cost a hung run to learn.
122	
123	Two practical notes. `--time-limit` counts **trace** time, not wall time: a 45-second budget is
124	roughly ten minutes of waiting, because the clock only advances while the page is busy. And the run
125	mutates data — Exclude/Include and the edit dialog's Save both write — so re-run `db:fresh` between
126	sessions.
127	
128	See [the spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
129	
130	## What still is not local
131	
132	- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
133	  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
134	  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
135	- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
136	  your machine.
137	
138	## Troubleshooting
139	
140	- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.

1	# Demo Data Seed
2	
3	A re-runnable script that populates a self-contained **"Sample Family (DEMO)"**
4	in the **local** Supabase stack, so the running app can be logged into for
5	documentation screenshots/videos and manual exploratory testing.
6	
7	> **Local only.** The demo family was also seeded into the remote project until
8	> 2026-07-26, when it was torn down there and the remote scripts were removed.
9	> `readConfig()` now refuses any non-loopback target.
10	
11	It is deliberately **image-free**: every seeded receipt has
12	`receipt_image_path = null`, so receipts render in their placeholder state
13	("No image" / "(manual)"). See the note on that below.
14	
15	> **Reuse:** the seed is written so a future automated test harness can reuse
16	> the same fixtures. That harness is **not** built yet — this is a dev utility
17	> today.
18	
19	## Logins
20	
21	| Role   | Email                        |
22	| ------ | ---------------------------- |
23	| Owner  | `sample.parent@example.com`  |
24	| Member | `sample.partner@example.com` |
25	
26	Both share one family and one **fixed password**, `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
27	`scripts/demo/credentials.ts`, also printed at the end of each seed run.
28	`@example.com` is an IANA-reserved documentation domain — it accepts no mail and
29	can't collide with real accounts.
30	
31	The password used to be randomly generated per run. It is a checked-in constant
32	now so local tooling can log in unattended, which is only safe because the demo
33	account cannot exist anywhere but a loopback stack — see the guard below.
34	
35	**The app itself logs in as the owner during local development.**
36	`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` signs in at boot, gated on `import.meta.env.DEV` _and_
37	a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, so Bombadil (which has no way to authenticate
38	itself) gets a real session. It skips `/login`, `/forgot-password` and
39	`/reset-password`, so the logged-out screens are still reachable by hand and a
40	manual logout is not instantly undone. See
41	[the Bombadil spike](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
42	
43	## Commands
44	
45	```bash
46	npm run seed:demo            # auto-clean any prior demo data, then rebuild
47	npm run seed:demo:teardown   # delete the demo users + demo family
48	npm run db:fresh             # db:reset && seed:demo — the whole known state
49	```
50	
51	Both wrap `local:env`, which injects Supabase's fixed local defaults, so neither
52	needs 1Password. They need:
53	
54	- `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the target stack (echoed on start).
55	- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — full-access key; required to create the auth
56	  users (Admin API) and to insert RLS-protected rows. The scripts hard-fail with
57	  a clear message if either is missing.
58	
59	## The local-only guard
60	
61	`readConfig()` rejects any `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` whose hostname is not loopback,
62	before the service-role client is built. That is what makes a checked-in
63	password acceptable: seeding a remote project would plant a known credential in
64	it, so "don't do that" is enforced rather than agreed. Relaxing the guard means
65	reinstating a generated password.
66	
67	A full local wipe is `npm run db:reset` — `seed:demo:teardown` exists for
68	removing just the demo family while leaving the rest of your local data intact.
69	
70	`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
71	run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
72	demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
73	artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
74	stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).
75	
76	**Teardown order matters:** `teardownDemo()` must delete the **auth users before
77	the family**. `receipts.family_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and receipts only
78	cascade via `receipts.user_id` — so deleting the family first leaves the demo
79	receipts alive with a nulled `family_id`, invisible to the name-scoped cleanup
80	and un-removable by a re-run.
81	
82	## What it creates
83	
84	- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
85	  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
86	  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
87	  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.
88	- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
89	  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
90	  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
91	  toggle.
92	- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
93	  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
94	- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
95	  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
96	  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
97	  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
98	  uncategorized.
99	
100	The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
101	produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.
102	
103	## The no-image consequence
104	
105	Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
106	the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
107	blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
108	intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
109	few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

113	- `scripts/demo/credentials.ts` — the demo identity (emails, family name,
114	  password) and the loopback check. **Dependency-free on purpose**: the app's
115	  dev auto-login imports it, and must not drag the service-role client into the
116	  browser bundle to do so.
117	- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
118	- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
119	- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
120	- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

122	Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).

# Local development

A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.

## One-time setup

1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.

   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
   itself.

2. `npm install`

## Daily use

```bash
npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
npm run dev          # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
```

| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
| `npm run db:fresh`         | `db:reset` then `seed:demo` — back to a known state in one command   |
| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
| `npm run dev:remote`       | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
| `npm run seed:demo`        | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |
| `npm run bombadil`         | Property-based UI exploration of `/transactions` (see below)         |

`dev` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
1Password. Only `npm run dev:remote` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.

**Local is the default now.** `npm run dev` pointed at production until 2026-07-26; the names were
swapped so the safe target is the one you get by reflex. Demo data is local-only for the same
reason — see [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

Note that `dev` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints the login
to use. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:fresh`.

**You will already be logged in.** In dev, against a loopback stack, the app signs itself in as the
demo owner at boot (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`) — it exists so Bombadil, which cannot authenticate
itself, gets a real session. Two gates, for two reasons: `import.meta.env.DEV` is what keeps the
password out of the production bundle (verified — it is dead-code-eliminated), and the loopback
check is what stops `dev:remote`, which is also DEV, from firing demo credentials at production. To
see the logged-out screens, go to `/login` directly; the auto-login skips the auth routes, so a
manual logout sticks.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## Property-based UI exploration (Bombadil)

```bash
npm run db:fresh     # known starting state — --reproduce depends on it
npm run dev          # in another terminal
npm run bombadil     # explore /transactions; exit 2 means a property was violated
npm run bombadil:inspect
```

Antithesis's [Bombadil](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html) drives
the page at random and checks the properties in `bombadil/transactions.ts` after every action. That
file is the interesting part — read its header before changing it, because most of what is _not_ in
it (the header, the file input, every `<select>`, the Delete buttons) is excluded for a reason that
cost a hung run to learn.

Two practical notes. `--time-limit` counts **trace** time, not wall time: a 45-second budget is
roughly ten minutes of waiting, because the clock only advances while the page is busy. And the run
mutates data — Exclude/Include and the edit dialog's Save both write — so re-run `db:fresh` between
sessions.

See [the spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

input.old_string:
## Remaining work

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + hook in `src/routes/+layout.svelte:28`.**
   Must complete _before_ `authChecked = true`, or the layout briefly treats the
   user as logged out and the run starts with a redirect flap.

   Gate on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops plain
   `npm run dev`… — which is now local, but `dev:remote` is still DEV — from firing
   demo credentials at production.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`. Reset-to-known-state matters
   more here than in normal dev: `--reproduce` only replays faithfully from an
   identical starting state, and the docs are explicit that reproductions fail when
   "application state has changed".

3. **The specification** — `bombadil/transactions.ts`. Default properties only (no
   `export *`), a hand-written action generator confined to the page's own
   controls, the pathname tripwire, and the filter/sort properties above.

4. **Decide where it runs.** Local-only for now. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs.

## Suggested first run

Deliberately with **no specification file** — just to confirm the binary installs
and the free properties report before investing in a spec:

```bash
npm run db:up
npm run seed:demo
npm run dev                    # localhost:5173, no MISTRAL_API_KEY
npx bombadil browser test --time-limit 2m --output-path bombadil-out \
  http://localhost:5173/login
npx bombadil browser inspect bombadil-out   # timeline UI, violation markers
```

Then repeat against `/transactions` once auto-login lands, adding the spec file as
the final argument.
input.new_string:
## What was built

All landed 2026-07-26. `@antithesishq/bombadil@0.6.1` is a dev dependency; it has
**zero dependencies of its own** and ships prebuilt binaries.

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`**, awaited in `src/routes/+layout.svelte` before
   `authChecked = true` so the run doesn't start with a logged-out flap.

   Gated on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops
   `npm run dev:remote` — which points at production and is still DEV — from
   firing demo credentials at it. **Verified**: a production build contains
   neither the password, the demo email, nor the function name.

   It also skips `/login`, `/forgot-password` and `/reset-password`. That was not
   in the original plan and is worth keeping: it means a developer can still see
   the logged-out screens locally, and that `logout()`'s redirect to `/login` is
   not instantly undone — session loss stays visible rather than being papered
   over. This is _not_ the ruled-out "re-login on `SIGNED_OUT`"; nothing watches
   auth state, it only runs at boot.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`.

3. **`scripts/demo/credentials.ts`** — new. The demo identity and the loopback
   check moved out of `common.ts` into a **dependency-free** module so the
   browser can import the password without dragging the service-role client (and
   `process.env`) into the client graph. `common.ts` re-exports it, so the seed
   scripts are unchanged.

4. **`bombadil/transactions.ts`** — the specification. 12 properties: the 4 free
   ones, the pathname tripwire, and 7 hand-written. `npm run bombadil` and
   `npm run bombadil:inspect` wrap the CLI; `bombadil/**/*.ts` was added to
   `tsconfig.json` so `npm run check` covers it; `/bombadil-out/` is gitignored.

5. **Where it runs:** local-only, unchanged. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs, but there
   is no CI at all yet — see the backlog item for that.

### The properties

Beyond the four free ones and `pageIsAlwaysTransactions`:

| Property                             | What it would catch                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `noRowFallsOutsideTheDateFilter`     | The filter itself. Both bounds live in the URL, so filter and rows are both observable — the only one of the four filters that is. |
| `rowCountMatchesTheShowingCounter`   | "Showing N of M" disagreeing with the table, or N > M                            |
| `selectAllReflectsTheRows`           | `isAllSelected` / `isIndeterminate` vs. the rendered tri-state checkbox          |
| `selectionButtonsMatchTheSelection`  | Delete Selected (N) / Clear Selection enabled with nothing selected, or N < ticked rows |
| `anEmptyTableExplainsItself`         | A filter emptying the table and leaving a blank slab, with neither empty state   |
| `editDialogCanAlwaysBeClosed`        | The dialog losing its only exit (it has no backdrop-click or Escape handler)     |
| `importIsNeverTriggered`             | The spec accidentally reaching the file input                                    |

Vendor / amount / card-type filters have **no** property, deliberately: their
_applied_ values live in component state and never reach the DOM, so only the
temp input values are observable and there is nothing to check them against.

## What the runs taught

Four things that only showed up by running it, each of which cost a wedged run:

1. **`PressKey` wedges the browser.** Every run including it hung — Chrome pinned
   at 100% CPU, Bombadil idle at 0%, waiting for an event that never arrived. The
   worst froze two actions in, on the first key. Removing it took the same
   specification from ~25 actions before a hang to **391 actions in a clean
   60-second run**. The mechanism is unidentified; this is an empirical
   exclusion, not a diagnosis, and worth retrying on a later release.

   This also invalidated an intermediate conclusion worth recording so nobody
   re-derives it: the runs looked *slow*, and they were not. They were fast right
   up to the point they wedged. Roughly **5 actions/second** is the real rate.

2. **Native `<select>` popups hang it too**, for an understandable reason: Chrome
   renders the option list outside the page, so no DOM-derived click and no
   synthesized key can reach or dismiss it. Both selects are excluded, which
   costs coverage of the card/bank-type filter.

3. **"In the viewport" is not "clickable".** Bombadil dispatches at a coordinate,
   and the layout's `sticky top-0` header floats over the top ~53px of the
   scrolled page. A row checkbox that had scrolled under it produced a point that
   landed on a nav link, and the run left for `/receipts`. Fixed with an
   `elementFromPoint` hit test in `clickPoint`. **The tripwire is what caught
   this** — without it the run would have quietly spent 124 states on the wrong
   page. It is the single most valuable property in the file.

4. **Properties are evaluated from the very first state**, before the app has
   rendered anything. `always(…)` includes the "Loading…" frame, so every
   property has to tolerate a page that does not exist yet — the `settled` flag
   in the `table` extractor exists only for that.

One more, cheap to miss: extractors run on **every** state and may only return
JSON. On a ~100-row page, per-element `getBoundingClientRect` / `getComputedStyle`
is the dominant cost, so all targets come from one DOM pass and rows are rejected
by their own rectangle before their cells are ever measured.

### Reading a run

`exit 0` = clean, `2` = property violated, `1` = error. **Once
`pageIsAlwaysTransactions` fires, stop reading**: exploration has left the page,
so every later state violates it too and the other properties are being checked
against the wrong screen. Fix the escape and re-run.

A run **mutates data** — Exclude/Include and the dialog's Save both write — so
`npm run db:fresh` between sessions, which `--reproduce` needs anyway.

All landed 2026-07-26. `@antithesishq/bombadil@0.6.1` is a dev dependency; it has
**zero dependencies of its own** and ships prebuilt binaries.

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`**, awaited in `src/routes/+layout.svelte` before
   `authChecked = true` so the run doesn't start with a logged-out flap.

   Gated on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops
   `npm run dev:remote` — which points at production and is still DEV — from
   firing demo credentials at it. **Verified**: a production build contains
   neither the password, the demo email, nor the function name.

   It also skips `/login`, `/forgot-password` and `/reset-password`. That was not
   in the original plan and is worth keeping: it means a developer can still see
   the logged-out screens locally, and that `logout()`'s redirect to `/login` is
   not instantly undone — session loss stays visible rather than being papered
   over. This is _not_ the ruled-out "re-login on `SIGNED_OUT`"; nothing watches
   auth state, it only runs at boot.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`.

3. **`scripts/demo/credentials.ts`** — new. The demo identity and the loopback
   check moved out of `common.ts` into a **dependency-free** module so the
   browser can import the password without dragging the service-role client (and
   `process.env`) into the client graph. `common.ts` re-exports it, so the seed
   scripts are unchanged.

4. **`bombadil/transactions.ts`** — the specification. 12 properties: the 4 free
   ones, the pathname tripwire, and 7 hand-written. `npm run bombadil` and
   `npm run bombadil:inspect` wrap the CLI; `bombadil/**/*.ts` was added to
   `tsconfig.json` so `npm run check` covers it; `/bombadil-out/` is gitignored.

5. **Where it runs:** local-only, unchanged. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs, but there
   is no CI at all yet — see the backlog item for that.

### The properties

Beyond the four free ones and `pageIsAlwaysTransactions`:

| Property                             | What it would catch                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `noRowFallsOutsideTheDateFilter`     | The filter itself. Both bounds live in the URL, so filter and rows are both observable — the only one of the four filters that is. |
| `rowCountMatchesTheShowingCounter`   | "Showing N of M" disagreeing with the table, or N > M                            |
| `selectAllReflectsTheRows`           | `isAllSelected` / `isIndeterminate` vs. the rendered tri-state checkbox          |
| `selectionButtonsMatchTheSelection`  | Delete Selected (N) / Clear Selection enabled with nothing selected, or N < ticked rows |
| `anEmptyTableExplainsItself`         | A filter emptying the table and leaving a blank slab, with neither empty state   |
| `editDialogCanAlwaysBeClosed`        | The dialog losing its only exit (it has no backdrop-click or Escape handler)     |
| `importIsNeverTriggered`             | The spec accidentally reaching the file input                                    |

Vendor / amount / card-type filters have **no** property, deliberately: their
_applied_ values live in component state and never reach the DOM, so only the
temp input values are observable and there is nothing to check them against.

## What the runs taught

Four things that only showed up by running it, each of which cost a wedged run:

1. **`PressKey` wedges the browser.** Every run including it hung — Chrome pinned
   at 100% CPU, Bombadil idle at 0%, waiting for an event that never arrived. The
   worst froze two actions in, on the first key. Removing it took the same
   specification from ~25 actions before a hang to **391 actions in a clean
   60-second run**. The mechanism is unidentified; this is an empirical
   exclusion, not a diagnosis, and worth retrying on a later release.

   This also invalidated an intermediate conclusion worth recording so nobody
   re-derives it: the runs looked *slow*, and they were not. They were fast right
   up to the point they wedged. Roughly **5 actions/second** is the real rate.

2. **Native `<select>` popups hang it too**, for an understandable reason: Chrome
   renders the option list outside the page, so no DOM-derived click and no
   synthesized key can reach or dismiss it. Both selects are excluded, which
   costs coverage of the card/bank-type filter.

3. **"In the viewport" is not "clickable".** Bombadil dispatches at a coordinate,
   and the layout's `sticky top-0` header floats over the top ~53px of the
   scrolled page. A row checkbox that had scrolled under it produced a point that
   landed on a nav link, and the run left for `/receipts`. Fixed with an
   `elementFromPoint` hit test in `clickPoint`. **The tripwire is what caught
   this** — without it the run would have quietly spent 124 states on the wrong
   page. It is the single most valuable property in the file.

4. **Properties are evaluated from the very first state**, before the app has
   rendered anything. `always(…)` includes the "Loading…" frame, so every
   property has to tolerate a page that does not exist yet — the `settled` flag
   in the `table` extractor exists only for that.

One more, cheap to miss: extractors run on **every** state and may only return
JSON. On a ~100-row page, per-element `getBoundingClientRect` / `getComputedStyle`
is the dominant cost, so all targets come from one DOM pass and rows are rejected
by their own rectangle before their cells are ever measured.

### Reading a run

`exit 0` = clean, `2` = property violated, `1` = error. **Once
`pageIsAlwaysTransactions` fires, stop reading**: exploration has left the page,
so every later state violates it too and the other properties are being checked
against the wrong screen. Fix the escape and re-run.

A run **mutates data** — Exclude/Include and the dialog's Save both write — so
`npm run db:fresh` between sessions, which `--reproduce` needs anyway.

Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.

## Target page: `/transactions`

`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.

Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
disagree.

**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
less state worth exploring.

**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs.

## Prerequisites — done

Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:

- Demo family torn down in production; verified by direct SQL (demo users, demo
  family, and orphan sweeps across every family/user-scoped table plus
  `storage.objects` — all zero).
- `readConfig()` hard-fails on any non-loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, before the
  service-role client is built.
- Demo password is now the checked-in constant `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
  `scripts/demo/common.ts` (`DemoFamily-2026!local`), verified to authenticate
  against the local stack.
- Script names simplified — `npm run dev` and `npm run seed:demo` are the local
  ones; production is the explicit `npm run dev:remote`.
- `npm run check` now type-checks `scripts/` and `e2e/`, which it never did before.

See [Demo data seed](../demo-seed.md) and [Local development](../local-dev.md).

  next: it costs us Backspace, Escape and arrow-key interaction, which is real

1	# Bombadil Property-Based UI Testing — Spike Handoff
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-26
4	**Status:** 🟢 **Built and running.** The auto-login, `db:fresh` and
5	`bombadil/transactions.ts` all landed on 2026-07-26; a clean 60-second run
6	explores ~250 actions with no property violations. Everything below the
7	research sections is now a record of what was built and what the runs taught,
8	not a plan — see [What was built](#what-was-built) and
9	[What the runs taught](#what-the-runs-taught).
10	
11	## The question
12	
13	Can we run [Bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil) — Antithesis's
14	property-based testing tool for web UIs — against **only** the local stack, scoped
15	to a **single page**, with **no receipts reaching Mistral**?
16	
17	**Answer: yes.** All three constraints are satisfiable. Two of them are not
18	satisfiable through Bombadil's own configuration, which is the main thing this
19	document exists to record.
20	
21	## Use the browser driver, not the terminal one
22	
23	The spike started from the wrong manual. Bombadil ships two independent drivers:
24	
25	| Driver      | Docs                                                                   | Drives                      |
26	| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
27	| **browser** | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html>  | Anything using the DOM      |
28	| terminal    | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/terminal/1-introduction.html> | TUIs over stdin/a text grid |
29	
30	We want **browser**. The terminal manual is a different tool for a different job
31	and nothing in it transfers.
32	
33	Useful pages: [specification language](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/3-specification-language.html),
34	[CLI reference](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/4-reference.html).
35	
36	## How it works
37	
38	A loop: extract DOM state → check every property → choose and perform an action →
39	wait for an event (navigation, DOM mutation, or timeout) → repeat. You supply
40	properties and action generators as a TypeScript ES module; Bombadil drives the
41	exploration.
42	
43	**Four properties come free with no specification at all**: uncaught exceptions,
44	unhandled promise rejections, error-level console logs, and HTTP 4xx/5xx
45	responses. Pointing it at a URL with no spec file is a genuinely useful first run.
46	
47	Specification vocabulary: `extract(state => …)` returns a `Cell<T>` read via
48	`.current`; formulas are built with `always` / `eventually` / `next` / `now`,
49	combined with `.and()` / `.or()` / `.implies()` / `.not()`, and time-bounded with
50	`.within(5, "seconds")`. Action generators are `actions(() => [...])` returning a
51	weighted tree, with `weighted([[10, a], [1, b]])` to bias exploration. Defaults
52	live at `@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults`.
53	
54	Version at time of writing: **v0.6.1**, published 2026-06-18 — comfortably clear of
55	our `.npmrc` `min-release-age=7`. Exit codes: `0` normal, `1` error, `2` property
56	violation.
57	
58	## Three findings that shape the design
59	
60	### 1. `<ORIGIN>` cannot scope to a single page
61	
62	The CLI argument is documented as _"Starting URL of the test (also used as a
63	boundary so that Bombadil doesn't navigate to other websites)"_ — the boundary is
64	**origin-level**, i.e. `http://localhost:5173`. Passing
65	`http://localhost:5173/transactions` will **not** stop it wandering into
66	`/expenses`, `/receipts` or `/profile`.
67	
68	Single-page confinement therefore has to come from the specification:
69	
70	- Do **not** `export * from "@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults"` — the defaults
71	  include general navigation and click-any-semantic-element generators. Re-export
72	  the default _properties_ only, and hand-write the action generator.
73	- Add a tripwire property (`always(() => location.pathname === "/transactions")`)
74	  so an escape is a loud violation rather than silent scope creep.
75	
76	### 2. There is no network interception, blocking, or mocking
77	
78	Nothing in the CLI or the specification language stubs outbound requests. Keeping
79	receipts away from Mistral is an application-level concern, and fortunately a
80	narrow one: the browser's **only** Mistral touchpoint is
81	`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` → `POST /api/ocr/extract`. A page that
82	never uploads a receipt never reaches it.
83	
84	Belt and braces: run the dev server with **no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`**. It is a dynamic
85	import (see the comment in `playwright.config.ts`), so the endpoint fails at
86	request time rather than build time — which turns the free "no 5xx responses"
87	property into a tripwire. If Bombadil ever finds a path to OCR, we get a
88	violation instead of a silent API bill.
89	
90	### 3. There is no authentication support
91	
92	No `--storage-state`, no cookie flag, no login helper. `--header` injects HTTP
93	headers only, which is useless here: `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` uses plain
94	`createClient` with `persistSession: true`, so the session lives in
95	**localStorage**.
96	
97	Two ways out, and we chose the second:
98	
99	- **`bombadil browser test-external --remote-debugger http://localhost:9222`** —
100	  launch your own Chromium, log in by hand, attach Bombadil to the live tab.
101	  Rejected: it depends on `--create-target=false` attaching to the _existing_
102	  authenticated tab, which the docs do not confirm, and it needs manual
103	  choreography before every run.
104	- **A dev-only auto-login** ✅ — establish a real Supabase session at boot. Auth
105	  stays fully intact, plain `bombadil browser test` works, and the run is
106	  reproducible from one command.
107	
108	Note this deliberately means Bombadil never explores the logged-out state or the
109	login page. Acceptable given the single-page scope; revisit if the scope widens.
110	
111	## Why not a true auth bypass
112	
113	Considered and rejected. Every protected page independently calls
114	`supabase.auth.getSession()`, and all reads are RLS-gated on `family_members`.
115	Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
116	whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
117	code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.
118	
119	## Target page: `/transactions`
120	
121	`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
122	state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
123	temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
124	toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.
125	
126	Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
127	filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
128	disagree. (The third turned out not to be an invariant — the temp inputs
129	legitimately diverge from the URL between editing and Apply. See the property
130	table below for what was built instead.)
131	
132	**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
133	so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
134	less state worth exploring. — _Resolved differently: both Delete paths call
135	`confirm()`, a browser dialog the action vocabulary cannot answer, so they are
136	excluded outright. Runs still mutate via Exclude/Include and the dialog's Save._
137	
138	**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
139	Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
140	Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
141	`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs. — _Both done. Scoping
142	the targets to `<main>` turned out not to be enough on its own; see finding 3._
143	
144	## Prerequisites — done
145	
146	Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
147	credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:
148

The spike is built and working. A clean 60-second run: **exit 0, 391 actions, zero violations**, every control group exercised.

## What landed

- **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`** + hook in `+layout.svelte`, awaited before `authChecked` flips. Gated on `import.meta.env.DEV` **and** a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. Verified: the production build contains neither the password, the demo email, nor the function name.
- **`scripts/demo/credentials.ts`** (new) — the demo identity moved out of `common.ts` into a dependency-free module, so the browser can import the password without pulling the service-role client into the client graph. `common.ts` re-exports it; seed scripts unchanged.
- **`npm run db:fresh`**, plus `npm run bombadil` / `bombadil:inspect`.
- **`bombadil/transactions.ts`** — 12 properties (the 4 free ones, the pathname tripwire, and 7 hand-written covering the date filter, the showing-counter, select-all tri-state, selection buttons, empty states, dialog escapability, and import-never-reached). Added to `tsconfig.json` `include`; `/bombadil-out/` gitignored.

## Four things only running it revealed

1. **`PressKey` wedges the browser** — Chrome pinned at 100% CPU, Bombadil idle. Three runs, three hangs; the last froze two actions in. Removing it took the same spec from ~25 actions to 391. Mechanism unidentified — an empirical exclusion, not a diagnosis. It also invalidated my intermediate "runs are slow" reading: they're fast (~5 actions/sec) right up to wedging.
2. **Native `<select>` popups hang it too** — Chrome renders the option list outside the page. Both selects excluded; the card/bank-type filter has no coverage as a result.
3. **"In the viewport" ≠ "clickable."** The `sticky top-0` header floats over the top ~53px, so a row checkbox scrolled under it produced a point that landed on a nav link and the run left for `/receipts`. Fixed with an `elementFromPoint` hit test. **The tripwire caught this** — it's the highest-value property in the file.
4. **Properties are evaluated from the very first state**, before the app renders — `always(…)` includes the "Loading…" frame.

## Two things to flag

- **A test regressed and is fixed.** `layout-render.svelte.spec.ts` broke because the layout now imports a second module reading `$env/static/public`, which vitest doesn't populate. Added a `vi.mock('$lib/dev/autoLogin', …)` and documented the boundary in `appMocks.ts`. Full suite green: 1437 unit + 9 e2e, `check` 0/0, lint clean.
- **`npm audit` now reports 9 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 4 high), 6 of them new since the last recorded audit** — including a critical in `@vitest/browser` (browser-mode file-access gate bypass) which we do use. None come from Bombadil (it has zero dependencies). All claim a fix via plain `npm audit fix`. Logged in `docs/product-backlog.md` → Dependencies; **not** fixed, since that's a separate bump-and-verify job.

Docs updated: the spike handoff (now a record rather than a plan), `local-dev.md`, `demo-seed.md`, and the backlog. Nothing committed.
